newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says telecom equal access start unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says telecom equal access start unchanged.

text.p: Malaysia has no immediate plans to bring forward an agreement to introduce equal access to international telephone networks but could do so if industry players agree, Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Monday.
"We are committed to implementing equal access by January 1, 1999. But if we can bring it forward, so much the better," Moggie told reporters after opening an electronics conference.
"We are always talking to them (the industry). If the parties agree we could bring it (equal access) forward," he said.

Equal access means that all of state telecommunications firm Telekom Malaysia Bhd's three million subscribers would be able to use alternative trunk and international networks offered by its Malaysian competitors.
Speculation that the deadline may be brought forward had affected Telekom stock in recent weeks. The stock was down 30 cents to 20.90 ringgit at midday on Monday.
